judgments.reasoning_cat1: The class of Guaranteed Employees is defined entirely by reference to persons 'to be identified on Attachments "1" and "2"' — a future-tense identification, and the attachments are not part of the document as produced. A definition that outsources its whole content to a missing list is intrinsically incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every other Appendix A provision (c052, c054, c055, c057) depends on those same missing attachments, and c057 adds a further class — Eligible Group I Employees who obtain guarantees under paragraph 4B — that is not on either attachment. The 'only those individuals listed' rule and the 4B exception pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Guaranteed the opportunity to work five straight time shifts per week' turns on 'opportunity', which is the classic battleground in work-guarantee clauses (offered work versus paid shifts), and 'guarantee period' is defined only elsewhere. Both terms are nameable and contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c056, which lets The Times 'utilize fully' guaranteed employees in inverse seniority order, and against c018/c019, which relieve The Times of replacing absent RSHs and let it eliminate situations. Whether the five-shift opportunity survives those management rights is a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guarantees vest 'upon completion of the process described in paragraph 4B', but 4B describes a replacement procedure that operates 'during the term of this Agreement', so the completion date is indeterminate on the face of the reference. That is a real, nameable timing ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.B (c017) says 'Once the replacement procedure has been completed, there shall be no less than 270 RSHS during the term of this Agreement', which implies completion is an event but never says when it occurs. Reconciling an ongoing procedure with a single vesting moment is precisely a Category 2 problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For as long as any named employee is employed by The New York Times' reads oddly — 'any' rather than 'such' would make one person's continued employment sustain everyone's guarantee — and 'within the scope of the present NMDU bargaining unit' fixes a snapshot that may drift. Both are visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'This provision shall survive the expiration of this Agreement' cuts against the fixed March 30, 2000 horizon in c001 and against c055, which caps parallel guarantees at the current CBA's expiration. A perpetual guarantee inside a term agreement is a real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until the expiration date of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement' is genuinely two-valued: the CBA expiring March 30, 1993, or that CBA as extended to March 30, 2000 by the preamble. Naming that term is straightforward and the stakes differ by seven years.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble (c001) both calls the pre-existing agreement 'the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which expires on March 30, 1993' and extends it to March 30, 2000, so the instrument itself supplies both readings. Compare also c054's contrary survival rule for Attachment '1' employees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Utilize fully the services of Guaranteed Employees before employing any additional employees' combined with 'in inverse seniority order' is internally awkward — utilising guaranteed employees junior-first is an unusual pairing whose practical rule is not obvious. 'Additional employees' is also undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Memorandum elsewhere allocates work by seniority bidding (c019) and the Edison staffing letter (c076) also uses inverse seniority, so the ordering rules across the instrument are not uniform. Read with c052's five-shift guarantee, the utilisation right and the guarantee can pull apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exclusivity rule ('shall apply only to those individuals listed') immediately qualified by an exception ('except for Eligible Group I Employees who obtain guarantees pursuant to paragraph 4B') — expressio unius against a stated carve-out. The reach of the carve-out is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.B (c017) says such employees 'shall have a length of contract employment guarantee governed by the terms of Appendix A', yet Appendix A's guarantees are framed entirely by the Attachment '1'/'2' lists this clause makes exclusive. That circularity is a checkable incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Suspension is keyed to circumstances 'under which RSH's are not entitled to be paid under the Collective Bargaining Agreement' — an external, unspecified set of circumstances. That is a soft boundary but at least anchored to a document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on terms of the underlying CBA carried forward by c001, which is not reproduced here, and sits alongside c059 and c061 as three different ways guarantees can end. The trio is arranged coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permanent suspension of the Newspaper' uses a capitalised term that is nowhere defined, and 'permanent' is a judgment call at the moment it must be applied. Short but genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contrasts with c058's temporary suspension of 'the delivery department's operations', so the two suspension triggers use different subjects and different consequences. That is a mild but real drafting seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For any reason, including but not limited to' followed by an illustrative list is a standard open catch-all, and 'terminates employment' would ordinarily cover involuntary discharge as well. The general/specific point is available but weak.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with c043's surrender of the guarantee on buyout and with c054/c055's employment-linked durations. No contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination of guarantees requires that a violation 'continues notwithstanding the issuance of a temporary restraining order by a court after a hearing' — a compound condition, but each element is concrete. 'Any violation' is broad against that narrow procedural gate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the No-Strike clause contained in this Memorandum' from within Appendix A, a separately executed agreement, and it must be squared with c027, under which the Union may lawfully be released from the no-strike obligation. Whether a released strike triggers forfeiture is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any labor organization' is immediately followed by a parenthetical list of nine named unions — the classic general-versus-specific problem — and the provisos turn on 'a wage package which is additional to or different from', 'productivity improvements or attrition exceeding that which is contained in' the Memorandum, and wages 'diverted from an existing or subsequently negotiated wage package', all of which are contestable measures. This is the most open-textured clause in the letter package.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the Union a route to a different wage package that runs alongside the c032 reopener and arbitration, and its own arbitration sentence funnels disputes to the Contract's grievance procedure administered by the Merits Arbitrator (c005). The overlap with the reopener is not addressed anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, concrete undertaking to file papers 'promptly upon notification' of ratification; 'promptly' is the only softness. Nothing meaningful to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated at the end of the package (the second identical injunction letter) with no divergence, and depends on c035's ratification condition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The 43rd Street and/or the staging facility' uses 'and/or' for an exclusion and names 'the staging facility' with a definite article though no staging facility is identified anywhere. Which locations are carved out is therefore genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 'all references to "new and rebuilt facilities"' in the Memorandum, directly qualifying c002, c003 and c004 — including the interest-arbitration route for new-facility disputes. That express, instrument-wide override is exactly the kind of cross-document tension Category 2 targets.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Forty (40) of the current Saturday Night Bulldog finishing times will be assigned to the forty (40) remaining routes' does not say which forty or by what method, and 'throughout the duration of this contract' fixes them indefinitely. The selection gap is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6 (c021) makes the SNBD reorganisation 'subject only to' the forty-route minimum, and c022 moves start times to no later than 4:00 p.m.; freezing finishing times contradicts the 'subject only to' language and interacts with the start-time change. That is a specific conflict with two identified provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shortfalls that may exist between shift contributions needed to maintain benefits status' turns on an external, undefined benefits-status standard, and the top-up obligation is open-ended. The measure of the shortfall is not fixed by the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It draws first on the 3.A.(3) contributions in c011, which that clause says are 'in lieu of and not in addition to' contributions otherwise due, and c069 and c074 separately raise and lower the same 450-FTE pool. Layering four adjustments on one contribution stream is a real reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel to c066 but simpler — 'separate contributions' to fund shortfalls — with the same undefined 'benefit status' measure. Moderate softness only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with c013's pension contributions for buyout takers and with c033's reapportionment right, which could change the pension rate that defines a shortfall. Worth checking; no flat contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole obligation is conditioned on the individuals' 'willingness ... to avail themselves of all work opportunities that may exist at The New York Times' — a subjective, unbounded condition whose failure defeats funding entirely. 'All work opportunities' is exactly the kind of term parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies both c066 and c067, and interacts with c018/c019, under which The Times need not create or fill work, so the very opportunities the employee must accept may not exist. That interplay is a genuine seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is arithmetically explicit — the minimum FTE contributions increase by the excess of employed FTEs over 370 — and the window is defined by ratification and 'full commencement of operations at Edison'. That last phrase is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends c011's 450-FTE minimum upward while c074 amends it downward and c066 draws on it, and it uses a 370 baseline drawn from the manning provisions (c016) rather than the 450 figure in 3-A(3). Squaring 370, 450 and the two adjustments is a live whole-instrument issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dedicated school and college routes may be added as needed' and suspension or abolition 'at the discretion of The Times' are broad discretions, but the shift times and the revert-to-11:30 p.m. rule are concrete. Moderate-low exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates route and start-time rules that sit alongside the reorganisation rights in c020 and c023 and the guarantee of five shifts in c052 without express reconciliation. Nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will make every effort within its control to insure' is a best-efforts formulation doubly hedged, and 'bootlegging' is put in quotation marks without definition. Both the standard and its object are open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers jurisdiction back to the underlying Collective Bargaining Agreement carried forward by c001, which is not reproduced, so its content depends on an external document. No conflicting provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite deadline and a definite committee composition; nothing to construe. The purpose clause is general but does not create obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is completed by c073, which states the committee's charge, and it is triggered by ratification consistently with c035. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specifically charged with administering the transfer process' says what the committee does without saying what powers it has or how deadlocks resolve — vague in scope but not in meaning. Modest exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The committee is two-and-two (c072) with no tie-breaker anywhere in the instrument, and no provision routes committee deadlocks to the Merits Arbitrator (c005). That gap is worth noting but is an omission rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It promises 1996 contributions for one group and then reduces the 450-FTE-based contributions by the number of 1996 shifts, with the reduction 'evenly distributed throughout the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995' — spreading a 1996 figure backwards over four earlier years is mechanically incoherent on its face. The 'age sixty (60) or below' cut-off is at least definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly rewrites c011's minimum of 450 Full Time Equivalents for 1992-1995, the same figure c069 increases and c066 draws on, and c033 lets the Union reapportion the underlying rates. Four provisions adjusting one contribution stream in different directions is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to take 'the steps necessary to effectuate amendments' — a cooperation covenant with no specified content or deadline. Vague, but of the kind rarely fought over on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly serves paragraph 3-A(3) (c011) and this letter (c074), so it inherits whatever inconsistency those carry rather than creating its own. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The most junior qualified situation holder' assigned 'on an inverse seniority basis' pending 'final award' uses several terms of art without definition, and 'vacant, newly created, or temporary situations' is a list whose members are then treated identically. Moderate exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the assignment rule first, but c078 says the Chapel Chairman volunteer procedure must precede it ('Prior to instituting the procedure above'), so the sequence within the same letter has to be reconstructed. That ordering tension is specific and checkable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence — 'They shall be permanently assigned to permanent or vacant positions in the event those situations are not filled by bid' — is grammatically loose about which situations and which people, sitting immediately after a rule restoring them to their former situation. The two sentences point in different directions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause c078 repeats a near-identical bid-failure rule ('the most junior qualified situation holder will be permanently assigned to the vacancy and the volunteer shall return to his regular situation'), so the same event is governed twice in the same letter. Whether they say the same thing is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It opens 'Prior to instituting the procedure above' yet describes the volunteer route as a precondition, and the sentence about the volunteer filling the situation within seven days sits awkwardly with the later 'not filled by bid' fallback. The internal sequence is muddled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reorders c076 and duplicates the fallback rule in c077, and its three- and seven-day clocks must fit the four-day notice in c077. Reconciling the three provisions requires rearranging the letter as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Foreseen to be of two (2) weeks or less duration' depends on a prediction and does not say who forecasts it, which is a small but nameable softness. The exclusion is otherwise crisp.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out of c076-c078 and is consistent with them; no other provision addresses short vacancies. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence option to fill knock-on vacancies; the discretion is express and clear. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Edison staffing letter (c076-c079) and echoes The Times' discretion to fill or eliminate situations in c019. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The NMDU may, within 72 hours, discuss the possibility of employment opportunities' creates only a right to talk, within a startlingly short window, and 'impacted employees' is undefined — the provision may be illusory. Whether it obliges The Times to anything is exactly the argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Appendix A guarantees and the manning caps in c016/c017, which would constrain any hiring of outside employees, but nothing directly contradicts it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named individual, a named position, defined days off and a stated start time; nothing is open. No term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a one-off grievance settlement standing apart from the manning and bidding provisions, though a fixed award may bypass the seniority bidding in c019. No genuine conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, unambiguous release — withdrawal 'with prejudice' in consideration of the settlement. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It completes c082 and does not touch any other provision of the instrument. Very low.
